scenes.say: Ever wonder why Swift async code feels so much cleaner now? Let's see what concurrency brings to the table.

scenes.label: async/await
scenes.sub: Async and await make asynchronous code readable and safer.
scenes.say: Swift five point five added async and await. That means your asynchronous code is now much easier to read and debug.
Actors isolate shared data to prevent bugs. Main actor makes sure UI updates happen safely on the main thread.
Here's an actor that safely manages a counter. And a function marked main actor, so UI changes never break thread safety.

scenes.question: Can you update UI from any thread?
scenes.wrong: Yes, threads don't matter for UI.
scenes.right: No. UI updates must happen on the main actor to avoid crashes and glitches.
scenes.say: Interviewers love to ask about UI threads. Don't fall for it—always update user interface on the main actor.
